stories.title: Zimmet Law Group Signs 10-Year Lease for 515 Madison Ave.
stories.excerpt: GFP Real Estate announced that Zimmet Law Group P.C. has signed a new office lease for 5,476 square feet at 515 Madison Ave. in Manhattan’s Plaza District. Zimmet Law Group will occupy Suite 603 on the sixth floor of the building under a new 10-year lease, relocating its Manhattan office from 477 Madison Ave. The firm is expected to take occupancy following completion of its new space later this year. Martin McGrath and Kephra Stone of GFP Real Estate represented the landlord in-house. Elliot Zelinger of Savitt Partners represented Zimmet Law Group. “Zimmet Law Group’s decision to make a long-term commitment to 515 Madison Avenue speaks to the continued appeal of the building and the strength of the Plaza District,” said McGrath. “Professional services firms continue to prioritize high-quality, well-located office space, and we’re pleased to welcome Zimmet Law Group to the building.” The post Zimmet Law Group Signs 10-Year Lease for 515 Madison Ave. appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Zimmet Law Group signs 10-year, 5,476 sq ft lease at 515 Madison Ave, Manhattan Plaza District.
Professional services firm relocates from 477 Madison Ave, taking occupancy later in 2025.
Landlord rep cites continued appeal of Plaza District and strength of high-quality office demand.
stories.summary: Zimmet Law Group P.C. has committed to a decade-long lease for 5,476 square feet at 515 Madison Ave in Manhattan's Plaza District, relocating from nearby 477 Madison Ave. The deal signals sustained tenant demand for premium, well-located Manhattan office space. Occupancy is expected later this year.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. Office leasing strength in Plaza District may indicate broader Manhattan corporate stability, but does not materially affect residential supply, demand, or cost trajectories in primary multifamily submarkets.

stories.title: Avison Young Recapitalization Provides “War Chest” for Further Growth
stories.excerpt: Avison Young’s newly announced recapitalization does more than deleverage the company’s balance sheet debt-to-EBITDA ratio to less than 3x, reduce debt and preferred equity by nearly 70% and give key financial partners a common equity position, although it accomplishes all of these. “We’re pretty excited,” Avison Young chair and CEO Mark E. Rose told Connect CRE. “This gives us the war chest to do the things that we’re known for”–namely, make strategic acquisitions, broaden the platform’s capabilities and expand the pool of talent through recruitment. “And we have our eyes on targets.” Expected to close in October, the new transaction builds upon the success of the company’s 2024 recapitalization. It also represents a rethinking of how to produce the best outcome for Avison Young’s longtime financial stakeholders as well as the company’s principals.   “It’s kind of simple,” said Rose. “Was it better to take the money and pay these [stakeholders], or was it better to invest and make them multiples of the same money? And after 16 months, that’s what we were able to come to.”  The process of devising this solution began in the spring of 2025, Rose said. The company looked at various options for taking the stakeholders’ investment and “putting it into a different form that would meet everybody’s needs.”  The solution entailed a 70% debt-to-equity swap, “giving us a debt-to-EBITDA ratio that’s under 3x so that we can build, effectively, a fund—a pool of capital along with additional new money that [the stakeholders] were putting in,” said Rose.  He continued, “What we needed to do was work with our financial stakeholders, convert them into equity holders.” Their ownership stake is
bullets: Avison Young recapitalization reduces debt-to-EBITDA below 3x, cuts debt and preferred equity by ~70%.
Expected close October 2025; positions firm with capital for acquisitions, platform expansion, and talent.
CEO Mark Rose signals intent to deploy 'war chest' for strategic growth and M&A.
stories.summary: Avison Young has announced a recapitalization expected to close in October that significantly deleverages the CRE services firm, reducing debt-to-EBITDA to under 3x and cutting total debt and preferred equity by approximately 70%. The transaction converts key financial partners to common equity holders. CEO Mark Rose indicated the strengthened balance sheet will fund strategic acquisitions and platform expansion.
stories.impact: Modest indirect impact: Avison Young's enhanced capital position and appetite for acquisitions may increase competitive pressure for brokerage and advisory mandates on multifamily development and disposition transactions, potentially reducing deal advisory margins for smaller firms. No direct effect on supply, demand, or cost.

stories.title: Local Owner-Operator Snags Pico-Robertson Apartment Property
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 1476 S Shenandoah St., a 16-unit multifamily property in Los Angeles. The property sold for $5.3 million, or $334,937 per unit. “Properties like this rarely become available in Pico-Robertson, especially those that have been held by the same ownership for more than two decades,” said Sam Liberow, senior managing director investments. “After 23 years of ownership, the offering generated six competitive offers, reflecting continued demand for well-located multifamily assets with large floor plans. The buyer plans to renovate units through natural tenant turnover while holding the property as a long-term investment.” Liberow, in Marcus & Millichap’s Encino office, marketed the property on behalf of the seller, 1476 Shenandoah Street LLC. He also procured the buyer, a local owner and operator. Built in 1966, the 17,653-square-foot property is situated on a 0.30-acre parcel in Los Angeles’ Pico-Robertson neighborhood. The post Local Owner-Operator Snags Pico-Robertson Apartment Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap closed 16-unit apartment sale at 1476 S Shenandoah St, Pico-Robertson Los Angeles for $5.3M ($334,937/unit).
Property held 23 years; generated six competitive offers; local owner-operator buyer plans hold-and-renovate strategy.
Well-located, larger floor plans in Pico-Robertson remain scarce and highly competitive.
stories.summary: A 16-unit multifamily property in Los Angeles's Pico-Robertson neighborhood sold for $5.3 million ($334,937 per unit) after 23 years of single ownership. The sale attracted six competitive bids, reflecting persistent demand for well-located assets with spacious units. The buyer, a local owner-operator, plans long-term hold with unit renovations during natural turnover.
stories.impact: Pico-Robertson's scarcity of available multifamily assets and sustained competitive bidding signal entrenched owner-operator hold-to-maturity strategies and limited near-term trading velocity in the submarket. For Trammell Crow, this indicates limited acquisition windows in established Pico-Robertson submarkets; new development or value-add repositioning in adjacent West LA micro-markets may be more tractable entry strategies.

stories.title: Grocery-Anchored Queens Retail Secures $32M Financing
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s New York Metro Debt + Equity team, led by Robert Delitsky and Charles Cotsalas, arranged $32 million in financing for Springnex Plaza, a 96,028-square-foot retail property located in the Springfield Gardens neighborhood of Queens. Delitsky and Cotsalas arranged financing on behalf of the owner, Mattone Group Springnex LLC, through Principal Financial Group. “Ownership developed Springnex Plaza in 2000 and they have done a fabulous job maintaining very strong occupancy,” Delitsky said. “Supermarket-anchored shopping centers like Springnex Plaza will continue to attract very strong lender interest in today’s market,” added Cotsalas. Springnex Plaza is a 100% occupied, multi-tenant, grocery-anchored retail center situated on approximately 5.58 acres. Serving the Springfield Gardens community for more than two decades, Springnex Plaza offers a complementary mix of grocery, dining, healthcare and service-oriented tenants. Anchored by Stop & Shop, It is home to a diverse roster of local and national retailers, including Ashley Stewart, IHOP Restaurant, and Northwell Health. The post Grocery-Anchored Queens Retail Secures $32M Financing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Northmarq arranged $32M financing for 96,028 sq ft Springnex Plaza, Springfield Gardens Queens via Principal Financial Group.
100% occupied grocery-anchored retail with Stop & Shop anchor, complementary dining, healthcare, service tenants.
Supermarket-anchored centers attracting strong lender interest in current market; property 20+ years established.
stories.summary: Northmarq's New York Metro team arranged $32 million in financing through Principal Financial Group for Springnex Plaza, a fully occupied 96,028-square-foot grocery-anchored retail center in Queens' Springfield Gardens neighborhood. Anchored by Stop & Shop and serving a 20+ year track record, the deal reflects continued lender appetite for stabilized, essential-service-oriented retail.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development. Retail financing availability and grocery-anchor stability may signal underlying demand resilience in Queens submarkets, but this article addresses retail capital flow, not residential supply or demand dynamics affecting apartment development feasibility or returns.

stories.title: Brixton Capital Launches Multifamily Investment-Management Platform
stories.excerpt: Brixton Capital’s Residential division has launched an integrated multifamily investment-management initiative designed to help institutional investors, family offices, lenders, joint venture partners and other owners improve the performance and value of complex multifamily assets. The initiative combines Brixton’s institutional investment and asset management capabilities with the operating expertise of its affiliate, United Apartment Group. “We see a meaningful opportunity to partner with owners and investment groups that have good real estate but need a different investment-management solution,” said Brixton VP of residential acquisitions Mark Mandala. “There are many multifamily assets where the underlying property remains fundamentally attractive, but the existing sponsor may not have the capital, operating infrastructure or institutional asset-management capabilities required for the next phase of ownership. We believe this is a particularly compelling opportunity because we are not simply offering another property management solution—we can bring together the investment strategy and the execution platform under one roof.” Brixton’s Residential division is particularly focused on multifamily assets where ownership is seeking a new investment-management or operating partner, or where the property requires a broader restructuring of its business plan. The post Brixton Capital Launches Multifamily Investment-Management Platform appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Brixton Capital Residential launches integrated multifamily investment-management platform combining acquisition and asset management expertise.
Partners with United Apartment Group affiliate for operating capabilities; targets complex assets needing restructuring or new sponsor.
Focus on properties with strong fundamentals but capital, infrastructure, or institutional gaps in current ownership.
stories.summary: Brixton Capital's Residential division has launched an integrated investment-management initiative designed to acquire and reposition complex multifamily assets where the underlying property is sound but the current sponsor lacks capital, operating infrastructure, or institutional asset-management capacity. The platform combines Brixton's institutional investment expertise with United Apartment Group's operating systems.
stories.impact: Indicates growing institutional capital targeting multifamily sponsors in distress or transition; raises competitive acquisition pressure on sponsor-level deals and suggests consolidation of fragmented mom-and-pop portfolios. Developers with operational integration capabilities and institutional backing may have acquisition advantage, but sellers of stabilized assets will face more sophisticated buyer pools and potentially firmer pricing.

stories.title: CoStar Closes $800M Cash Acquisition of New-Home Platform Zonda
stories.excerpt: CoStar Group, a leading provider of online real estate marketplaces, information, analytics and 3D digital twin technology, announced that it has completed its acquisition of Zonda, a new home-construction data, homebuilder software and residential real estate marketplace platform, for $800 million in cash. Zonda’s platform of proprietary lot-level construction and development data, which serves more than 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders and suppliers, gives CoStar a foothold in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market, according to the CoStar announcement. Based in Washington, D.C., Zonda generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. CoStar’s acquisition of the platform was first announced in May. “Zonda has built an exceptional business around information the homebuilding industry relies on every day,” Andy Florance, founder and CEO of CoStar, said in announcing the deal’s closing. “This is a massive market with a sophisticated group of builders, developers, lenders, investors and suppliers that need purpose-built information, analytics and marketing solutions. With the acquisition now complete, we have the opportunity to bring together Zonda’s proprietary new construction data, software and builder relationships with CoStar Group’s technology, analytics and marketplace capabilities.” The deal provides Arlington, Va.-based CoStar with new-home data and analytics from Zonda, which tracks new-home communities, land development, construction activity, home sales and builder operations at the lot level. In addition, Zonda-owned residential marketplaces NewHomeSource.com and Livabl join CoStar’s portfolio, expanding its consumer marketplace business specifically into new construction. bullets: CoStar completed $800M cash acquisition of Zonda new-home construction data and homebuilder software platform.
Zonda generated ~$170M revenue in 2025; serves 3,000+ homebuilders, developers, lenders, suppliers; covers $400B annual new-home sales market.
Acquisition gives CoStar foothold in homebuilder/developer data and intelligence; closes deal first announced May 2025.
stories.summary: CoStar Group completed its $800 million acquisition of Zonda, a new-home construction data and homebuilder software platform that generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025 and serves over 3,000 builders, developers, lenders, and suppliers. Zonda's lot-level construction and development data provides CoStar access to the $400 billion annual new-home sales market.
stories.impact: Significant for multifamily supply-side intelligence and competitive landscape: CoStar's acquisition of Zonda enhances its ability to aggregate and monetize lot-level supply, land pipeline, and homebuilder/developer transaction data across U.S. markets. This may increase data costs and competitive intelligence sharing friction for multifamily developers relying on CoStar platforms, and may intensify pricing power of CoStar's residential data products. Developers should monitor whether Zonda's land-supply and entitlement-tracking tools are integrated into CoStar's multifamily acquisition and market-analysis modules.

stories.title: Michael Troyanovsky of Regency Development Group: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: With a population of less than 6,000, little Bay Harbor Islands, Fla., is often overlooked – but not by Regency Development Group. Since 2020, the developer has been building residential projects in the coastal community near Surfside, Indian Creek and Bal Harbour. Regency has four active projects on the island, including the 33-unit La Maré Regency, the nine-unit La Maré Signature and the 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas. Commercial Observer recently caught up with Michael Troyanovsky, managing partner and vice president of the family company, to discuss the submarket’s success. The following conversation has been edited for length and clarity.   Commercial Observer: Why Bay Harbor Islands? What caught your interest about that submarket? Michael Troyanovsky: A really valid question, because there were other hot spot areas that a lot of people were gravitating to when we first started buying Bay Harbor. We came to the area, and we really felt like it had the most potential. It was always overlooked. It’s honestly the most amazing hidden gem. It’s surrounded by the most beautiful waters, a little nook in the center of Miami. It’s getting more and more discovered. Since then, we really integrated into the island, and we really got to know the local community, the local governments, because we have to work very closely with them on getting all the projects approved and making sure that it fits the neighborhood and demographic. We opened up a big sales office here, and we plan to stay here for the future. Who are you finding is the target demographic for your units? It’s a little bit of a mix demographic-wise, but I would say a lot of people who, whether it’s local or international, really want boutique building living. bullets: Regency Development Group has four active multifamily projects in Bay Harbor Islands, Florida (population <6,000) since 2020.
Projects include 33-unit La Maré Regency, 9-unit La Maré Signature, 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas; described as overlooked 'hidden gem.'
Small coastal Miami-area submarket surrounded by Surfside, Indian Creek, Bal Harbour; benefits from proximity and scarcity.
stories.summary: Regency Development Group, a family-owned developer, has been building residential projects in Bay Harbor Islands, Florida—a small coastal community near Surfside and Bal Harbour—since 2020. The firm currently has four active projects totaling at least 62 units, citing the submarket's overlooked status and strong fundamentals despite its tiny population.
stories.impact: Bay Harbor Islands (and adjacent coastal Dade County micro-markets) demonstrate sustained development interest driven by scarcity, affluent demographics, and proximity to established luxury submarkets (Bal Harbour, Surfside). For Trammell Crow, this signals persistent South Florida coastal infill demand and suggests acquisition-for-development windows remain constrained in micro-markets adjacent to established high-value communities; greenfield or repositioning opportunities in higher-supply South Florida metros (e.g., Broward, West Dade) may offer better risk/return profiles.

stories.title: JBL Asset Management Buys Retail Condo Near Miami Design District
stories.excerpt: Alta Developers sold off a retail condo near the Miami Design District for $17.3 million, property records show. JBL Asset Management purchased the 25,504-square-foot asset on the ground floor of the Quadro condo building. The property at 3900 Biscayne Boulevard faces train tracks, just east of the Miami Design District, an open-air, luxury mall. Quadro’s retail tenants include The Shade Store, 7th Avenue furniture store and Waterworks plumbing supply store. Hollywood, Fla.-based JBL is marketing a 2,358-square-foot suite as the last remaining retail space at the 407,498-square-foot condo building. Alta Developers completed the 200-unit building in 2019. The purchase comes as the 18-block Design District, one of the country’s highest-grossing upscale malls, is undergoing a major expansion. Earlier this week, its owners, entities tied to Miami-based Craig Robins and LVMH billionaire Bernard Arnault, scored a $125 million construction loan to build a Snøhetta-designed, mixed-use building. The joint venture also launched sales for Fouquet’s condo and hotel development, designed by Pritzker Prize winner David Chipperfield. Representatives for Alta Developers and JBL Asset Management did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: JBL Asset Management purchased 25,504 sq ft retail condo at 3900 Biscayne Blvd, Edgewater Miami for $17.3M.
Ground-floor condo in Quadro building; tenants include The Shade Store, 7th Avenue furniture, Waterworks; near Miami Design District.
Design District undergoing major expansion: $125M construction loan announced; Fouquet's mixed-use project (Chipperfield/Arnault/Robins JV) launching sales.
stories.summary: JBL Asset Management acquired a 25,504-square-foot retail condo at 3900 Biscayne Boulevard in Miami's Edgewater neighborhood for $17.3 million. The ground-floor space in Quadro is home to specialty retail tenants and sits adjacent to the Miami Design District, which is undergoing significant expansion including a $125 million construction loan for a mixed-use project.
stories.impact: Design District expansion (backed by Arnault LVMH capital and Robins development) signals intensifying upmarket residential and mixed-use density in Edgewater/Biscayne corridor. Multifamily developers should monitor whether expanded Design District retail, dining, and hospitality draws residential demand northward into Edgewater and Wynwood; this may open acquisition windows in transitional blocks along Biscayne Boulevard and near rapid-transit corridors currently undervalued relative to proximation to the Design District expansion.

stories.title: Now Is the Time to Buy in Commercial Real Estate: Morgan Stanley
stories.excerpt: Despite a bumpy economy and increasingly high Treasury yields, one global investment firm believes now is the time to pounce on U.S. commercial real estate. Commercial Observer spoke with Tony Charles, global head of research and strategy at Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing, who outlined the main takeaways from Morgan Stanley Investment Management’s mid-year 2026 real estate outlook. After a four-year recession, commercial real estate is now being repriced, giving investors a chance to acquire prime assets at low prices; supply is down across the board; and megatrends in AI, global supply chains, and aging demographics have opened up attractive entry points into infrastructure, retail and senior housing. “We certainly believe we’re entering the next up-cycle for real estate. It’s an attractive entry point,” Charles told CO in a Thursday interview. “And, given the repricing that’s now below replacement costs, we’re pretty confident in the next vintage of real estate investing.” Charles argued that the recent U.S. real estate downturn — which began in mid-2022 amid the Federal Reserve’s policy U-turn to hike interest rates coming out of COVID-19 — created “the longest downturn for real estate since the 1980s and early 1990s,” and that four years later, pricing is still down an average of 20 percent across the board. But he noted that “supply is down dramatically, so that’s obviously very helpful for real estate,” and that a strong structural macroeconomic backdrop — U.S. GDP grew 2.1 percent year-over-year in the second quarter of 2026 — has provided “a lot of green shoots that are beginning to show through.” He pointed out that CRE transaction activity increased 23 percent year-over-year in the U.S., institutional capital raising is up nearly 40 percent on the year, and that CRE debt originations are up around 20 percent year-over-year. bullets: Morgan Stanley RE Investing outlook: After 4-year recession, CRE repriced below replacement cost; supply down across sectors.
Megatrends (AI, supply-chain shifts, aging demographics) opening attractive entry points in infrastructure, retail, senior housing.
Tony Charles (Morgan Stanley global head of research) signals next up-cycle beginning; attractive entry point for institutional buyers.
stories.summary: Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing's mid-year 2026 outlook argues that after a four-year commercial real estate downturn, the market is entering the next up-cycle, with prime assets repriced below replacement costs and supply constrained. The firm identifies megatrends in AI, supply chains, and aging demographics as opening attractive entry points in infrastructure, retail, and senior housing.
stories.impact: CRITICAL SIGNAL: Morgan Stanley's optimism on CRE repricing and entry-point attractiveness validates the current risk-adjusted acquisition thesis for disciplined multifamily developers. Below-replacement-cost pricing combined with constrained new supply indicates strong relative value for repositioning and stabilized-asset acquisition in primary/secondary markets. However, competitive institutional capital (endowments, pension funds, foreign SWFs) is likely mobilizing simultaneously; developers must execute faster on sourcing, underwriting, and capital deployment to capture mispriced assets before rates stabilize and spreads compress.

stories.title: Whole Foods to Open Daily Shop at Murray Hill’s 509 Third Avenue
stories.excerpt: Whole Foods Market has leased a 9,000-square-foot retail space in Manhattan’s Murray Hill neighborhood. The 15-year deal occupies a ground-floor space and outdoor terraces at 509 Third Avenue, according to a memorandum of lease filed in city records Friday morning. The 35-story, 229-unit apartment tower, known as the Murray, was developed by Kahen Properties with Lalezarian Properties. A spokesperson for Whole Foods confirmed the lease in an email to Commercial Observer, but declined to share further details. Whole Foods’ newest Manhattan location will be on the smaller side. The store will follow the Amazon-owned grocer’s new Whole Foods Market Daily Shop format. The quick-trip urban shops sell grab-and-go meals alongside fresh produce, meat, bakery items and local specialty foods, according to the company’s website. The format was first rolled out in nearby Lenox Hill in 2024, and has since arrived in cities nationwide. Additional locations in Brooklyn and Hoboken, N.J., were announced late last year. Most recently, the grocer signed a lease for 8,121 square feet to open a daily shop at 1524 Second Avenue on the Upper East Side. Kahen Properties’ Majid Kahen signed the lease memorandum for the landlord, while Paul Hilliard, vice president of real estate at Whole Foods, signed for the grocer. It is unclear whether either party worked with an outside brokerage. The asking rent for the ground-floor space was not disclosed in the memorandum, but retail space in the nearby Herald Square area was $394 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026, according to CBRE data. Spokespeople for Kahen and Lalezarian Properties did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Whole Foods Market leased 9,000 sq ft at 509 Third Avenue, Murray Hill Manhattan; 15-year ground-floor + terrace deal.
Opening Whole Foods Market Daily Shop format (quick-trip urban store); first Lenox Hill location 2024; expanding Brooklyn, Hoboken.
Tenant in 35-story, 229-unit apartment tower (The Murray) developed by Kahen and Lalezarian Properties.
stories.summary: Whole Foods Market has signed a 15-year lease for 9,000 square feet at 509 Third Avenue in Manhattan's Murray Hill neighborhood. The location will operate under Whole Foods' newer Daily Shop format—a smaller, quick-trip urban store—and anchors ground-floor retail in The Murray, a 229-unit apartment tower developed by Kahen Properties and Lalezarian Properties.
stories.impact: POSITIVE SIGNAL for Murray Hill and upper East Side Manhattan multifamily demand: Whole Foods' commitment to Daily Shop expansion in Manhattan (Lenox Hill 2024, now Murray Hill, plus Brooklyn and Hoboken announcements) indicates sustained grocery/amenity infrastructure investment in residential neighborhoods. For Trammell Crow, this suggests that essential-service retail visibility and walkability—core multifamily amenity drivers in dense urban markets—remain attractive to premium grocers. Developers should prioritize ground-floor retail in Manhattan and secondary urban markets to capture tenant interest; grocery/prepared-food anchors command rents and drive foot traffic that enhance residential stabilization and lease-up velocity.
